- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (≥5% from prior day) with low sentiment (≤0.1), it often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- In high sentiment + rising price history, model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days ahead.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is below 70% of recent 5-day average, and sentiment is neutral or positive, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period price (last 7–10 days) — cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is high and price is flat or slightly falling, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
